newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine call rate drops on excess liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Philippine call rate drops on excess liquidity.

text.p: * Maturing T-notes to swamp already liquid market
The Philippine interbank call loan rate dropped to 10.90625 percent from Monday's 11.71875 percent on excess liquidity, traders said.

The system received 4.0 billion pesos worth of maturing Treasury notes in an already liquid market which was loaded by the Central Bank's heavy dollar purchases on the foreign exchange market in recent days.
Turnover in the interbank call market dwindled to only 17.744 billion pesos with done rates ranging from a low of 10.5625 percent to a high of 12.0 percent.
"It's a borrowers' market. There were so many banks trying to lend their money," one trader said.
There were 31 lenders as against 18 borrowing entities.
The secondary Treasury bill market was flooded with buyers. As a result, effective yields of T-bills slipped against yesterday's average auction rates.
Three-month bills were being bought at 11.95 percent, lower than the average 12.029 percent.
Six-month bills at 12.375 percent against 12.415 percent, and one-year bills at 12.95 percent from 13.015 percent.
Traders were also expecting the coupon rate for the five-year Treasury notes, which were to be auctioned in early afternoon, to drop to only 15.25 percent from the previous auction's 15.625 percent.
